prompt: Seismologists conclude that Earth's outer core is liquid partly because S-waves from earthquakes do not pass through it. Why do S-waves fail in a liquid?

options.text: Liquids are too dense for any seismic wave to enter
S-waves are transverse waves that need a rigid material that can support sideways shear, which a liquid cannot provide
S-waves are absorbed by iron, and the outer core is mostly iron
S-waves travel only along Earth's surface, never through the interior

explanation: S-waves shake material side to side. A liquid has no shear strength and cannot spring back from that sideways motion, so S-waves cannot propagate through the liquid outer core, creating an S-wave shadow zone.
